Mia Chen: Quick heads-up — zephyr-3b-embed int8 bring-up showing a measurable recall drop on wiki-holdout.
Mia Chen: baseline float32 recall@1 0.682 -> int8 0.634; recall@5 0.890 -> 0.861; silhouette 0.31 -> 0.24. Same index, same ANN params. Ran per-channel quant in ONNX and L2-normalized after quant.
Dmitri Ivanov: Did you rerun the normalization after quantization? int8 can change vector scale and break cosine distances.
Mia Chen: Yes, normalization applied post-quant. Snippet: ```python
# post-quant normalization
v = v / (np.linalg.norm(v) + 1e-12)
```
Mia Chen: Calibration set was ~10k diverse wiki passages. No prompt/template change.
Sara Lopez: Can you paste the exact eval command and seed? Also verify the ANN metric (cosine vs dot) — quant noise sometimes changes which metric is safe.
Mia Chen: Eval command I ran: `./eval_embeddings --model zephyr-3b-embed --index faiss_hnsw --metric cosine --holdout wiki --k 10 --quant int8 --norm l2 --seed 42`
embed-bot: Embed evaluation job 2419998765 completed — summary: baseline vs candidate diff uploaded to https://redwood.internal/embeds/evals/2419998765 (access: eng-ml)
Jon Park: Can you extract a handful of top-1 flip pairs (float32 neighbor != int8 neighbor)? If quant noise reorders neighbors it's easier to diagnose with sample pairs. Also check top-1 flip count and MRR change.
Mia Chen: Pasting 3 of the worst flip pairs (shortened):
- Q: "quantum computing intro"
  float32 top1: doc_472 (relevant)
  int8 top1: doc_1213 (less relevant)
- Q: "docker networking overlay"
  float32 top1: doc_88
  int8 top1: doc_204
- Q: "covid vaccine efficacy"
  float32 top1: doc_3100
  int8 top1: doc_3099
Mia Chen: Flip heatmap shows concentrated flips in a few dims (will attach).
Lee Nguyen: Try switching per-channel -> per-tensor quant and symmetric vs asymmetric zero-point. Per-channel often better but can introduce sign bias depending on calibration. Also check clamp and scale factors — if a dim has tiny variance, quant can zero it out.
Dmitri Ivanov: Another quick check: run float32 but add small gaussian noise (sigma ~ quant scale) to emulate quantization noise. If recall drop mirrors int8, it's quant noise, not runtime bug.
Sara Lopez: Also try disabling L2 normalization as an ablation — compare raw dot-product recalls vs normalized cosine. That can indicate whether magnitude perturbations drive the ranking changes.
Mia Chen: Confirmed prompt/template identical. Plan: run these jobs in parallel — (1) per-channel vs per-tensor, (2) symmetric/asymmetric, (3) float+noise ablation, (4) no-normalize ablation, (5) UMAP of sample clusters to visualize cluster collapse. Will attach results.
Jon Park: If per-channel fixes it, maybe add a small per-dim clipping or tiny smoothing during calibration to avoid zeroing dims. Also consider tiny post-quant calibration using a small heldout set to learn a diagonal rescale.
Sara Lopez: Nice. Also collect silhouette and mean intra/inter cluster distances for each run. Those numbers helped us spot similar issues before.
Mia Chen: Will run and post results in ~2 hours. ETA 2h. Thanks for the pointers. :thumbsup:
Lee Nguyen: If you want I can run the UMAP/TSNE viz and a quick nearest-neighbor flip scatter. Ping me the export.
Mia Chen: Thanks Lee — I'll upload an export to the thread link when ready.
Sara Lopez: Great, appreciate the quick triage.
Mia Chen: Upload will include: full eval CSV, flip counts, MRR diff, silhouette, UMAP PNGs, and the small calibration scripts.
embed-bot: Reminder: job artifacts will expire in 14 days unless archived.
Mia Chen: Noted — I'll archive the useful runs.
